To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mirroring is a social action that facilitates the joint achievement of a common interactional goal, rather than a behavioral manifestation or index of empathy, affiliation or rapport.
Sound imitation in naturally occurring conversation does not necessarily lead to affiliation, and that sound imitation can be used to achieve affiliation.
sound imitation is a social resource for building progressivity in interaction, and that sound mirroring in natural interaction is not automatic but a choice made by participants in the interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which people build rapport and affiliation in interaction.
the social organization of interaction.
the role of sound imitation in naturally occurring interaction, and how it contributes to the building of rapport.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mirroring behavior in naturally occurring interaction facilitates social collaboration and the achievement of joint goals, rather than rapport or affiliation as such.
sound imitation in conversation is a resource for the joint achievement of social action.
mirroring is a social phenomenon that can be understood as a resource in the achievement of social collaboration and joint action in interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sound mirroring is not a behavioral marker for rapport as such, but that sound mirroring can be a resource to build sociality and rapport.
mirroring is not the same as rapport.
we are social beings, but we do not need to be identical in our behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sound imitation is a resource for building social interaction, rather than an expression of interpersonal rapport.
sound mirroring in interaction is a resource that is used by participants in the course of their joint achievement of interaction.
the concept of mirroring needs to be redefined in terms of social interaction and sociality.
